_meta.title: Law domain graph — connectivity remediation (PROPOSAL ONLY)
_meta.purpose: Grounded feedback/reciprocal edges and redundant paths to remediate the findings from assets/js/energy-connectivity-audit.js (the audit module is domain-generic) run against assets/data/domains/law.json. This is a recommendation artifact; it does NOT modify any live graph.
_meta.discipline: Every proposed edge carries a concrete grounding (a canonical-nodes.json regulatory/anatomical fact OR the reciprocity of an existing law.json edge). Candidates that could not be grounded are omitted and tallied under _omittedForLackOfGrounding.
_meta.doNotApply: Do not merge these edges into assets/data/domains/law.json without an explicit apply step.
_meta.neuroReferenceThesis: Healthy circuits are ~80% recurrent/lateral; the network, not the node, is the unit of failure (diaschisis). A pure feedforward tree is the broken/cosmetic version.
_meta.pathologyVerdict: SAME SIGNATURE AS FINANCE, MORE FRACTURED. Law shows the identical core: ZERO reciprocal/feedback edges (recurrentFraction 0) despite carrying directed control rings, and it shares Finance's EXTRA fault — the graph is already split into 2 components at baseline, with the {M1, SMA} motor dyad fully disconnected from the main body. Law is MORE brittle than Finance on single-points-of-failure: 13 articulation nodes (Finance had 9), because the entire thalamo-sensory-motor cluster {THAL, V1, A1, S1, GP, CBLM, LGN, MGN, FEF} hangs off the main body through a single serial bridge chain STRI -> GP -> THAL.

recurrenceAudit.note: ZERO reciprocal/feedback edges — the same feedforward-only signature the neuro reference calls the broken version. The graph does carry directed cycles (the business-layer control ring BLA->TPJ->DMN->dACC->AG->CeA->BLA via CONTROLS+DEPENDS_ON edges), but for no edge A->B does B->A exist, so recurrentFraction is exactly 0. verdict from the module = 'has recurrent/lateral structure' only because lateralFractionOfClassifiable (0.314) clears the 0.2 lateral threshold; the feedback dimension is fully absent.

singlePointsOfFailure.baseComponentsNote: TWO components at baseline. Main body = 38 nodes; a fully disconnected dyad = {M1, SMA} (only internal edge SMA->M1, no edge in or out of the main body). This pre-existing fracture is the shared extra fault vs Energy (Energy baseComponents=1); Finance had the identical {M1, SMA} fracture.

mechanismOfEachArticulation.STRI: sole bridge of the ENTIRE thalamo-sensory-motor cluster {THAL, V1, A1, S1, GP, CBLM, LGN, MGN, FEF} to the main body — that cluster reaches the main body only via the serial chain FG->STRI->GP->THAL. Removing STRI severs the whole cluster.
mechanismOfEachArticulation.GP: second link on the same serial bridge chain (STRI->GP->THAL); removing GP also severs the thalamo-sensory-motor cluster from the main body.
mechanismOfEachArticulation.THAL: within the sensory cluster, sole attachment of leaf S1 (S1->THAL only), of leaf CBLM (CBLM->THAL only), of the auditory island {A1, MGN} (A1->THAL, MGN->A1), and of the visual island {V1, LGN, FEF} (THAL->V1 is its only link to the cluster spine).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.V1: sole attachment of leaf LGN (LGN->V1 only) and leaf FEF (FEF->V1 only).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.A1: sole attachment of leaf MGN (MGN->A1 only).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.OFC: sole attachment of the reward island {NAcc, VTA, VP} — NAcc->OFC is that island's only link to the main body.
mechanismOfEachArticulation.NAcc: within the reward island, sole attachment of leaf VTA (VTA->NAcc only) and leaf VP (NAcc->VP only).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.HIPP: sole attachment of leaf HPA (HPA->HIPP is HPA's only edge).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.vmPFC: sole attachment of leaf PAG (vmPFC->PAG is PAG's only edge).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.dACC: sole bridge of the interoceptive island {AI, NTS, PI} to the main body — AI->dACC is that island's only link out.
mechanismOfEachArticulation.AI: within the interoceptive island, sole attachment of leaves NTS (NTS->AI only) and PI (PI->AI only).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.dlPFC: sole attachment of leaf FPN (FPN->dlPFC is FPN's only edge).
mechanismOfEachArticulation.PVN: sole attachment of leaf HYPO (PVN->HYPO is HYPO's only edge).

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the value<->context loop; the context/valuation brake feeds back onto outcome valuation. Reciprocal of the existing OFC->vmPFC edge.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge OFC->vmPFC (excit). canonical-nodes vmPFC = M1 'top-down inhibitory brake', OFC = M6 'outcome valuation / update'; they are adjacent medial/orbital PFC regions with dense reciprocal connectivity.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the valuation<->reward loop; the outcome-valuation stage feeds back to the reward driver. Reciprocal of the existing NAcc->OFC edge.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge NAcc->OFC (excit). The orbitofrontal cortex is a principal glutamatergic corticostriatal input to the ventral striatum / nucleus accumbens (canonical OFC->NAcc projection). canonical-nodes OFC = M6 valuation, NAcc = M11 'incentive/reward drive'.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the conflict-monitoring -> cognitive-control loop: the conflict/error signal feeds back to the executive to adjust control gain.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge dlPFC->dACC (excit). canonical-nodes dACC = M6 'conflict/error monitor', dlPFC = 'dorsolateral PFC — executive working-memory / cognitive control'. dACC<->dlPFC are reciprocally connected (Botvinick conflict-control loop).

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the salience-network loop; the two salience hubs must be mutually coupled to co-select what gets escalated.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge AI->dACC (excit, 'interoceptive -> conflict monitor'). canonical-nodes AI = M10 'interoceptive salience'; the anterior insula and dorsal ACC are the two defining hubs of the salience network and are reciprocally coupled by definition.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Corticothalamic feedback closing the visual thalamo-cortical loop that THAL->V1 opens.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge THAL->V1 (excit, visual sensory relay). Layer-6 corticothalamic feedback V1->LGN/pulvinar is canonical and modulatory (feedback outnumbers feedforward). canonical-nodes THAL = M4 'gating relay / routing'.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Corticothalamic feedback closing the auditory thalamo-cortical loop that THAL->A1 opens.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge THAL->A1 (excit, auditory sensory relay). A1->MGN corticothalamic feedback is canonical and modulatory.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Corticothalamic feedback closing the somatosensory thalamo-cortical loop that THAL->S1 opens.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge THAL->S1 (excit, somatosensory relay). Layer-6 corticothalamic feedback S1->VPL is one of the most numerous projection classes in the brain, functionally gain/precision control -> modul.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the intra-amygdala threat loop that the existing CeA->BLA edge half-opens: the sensory/associative amygdala drives the central output nucleus.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge CeA->BLA (DEPENDS_ON). The basolateral -> central amygdala (BLA->CeA) projection is THE canonical intra-amygdala feedforward pathway (textbook fear circuit). canonical-nodes BLA = M7 'threat learning/acquisition', CeA = M7 'phasic fear output'.

proposedFeedbackEdges.rationale: Closes the conflict<->context loop; the conflict monitor feeds the ventromedial brake that it depends on. Reciprocal of the existing vmPFC->dACC edge.
proposedFeedbackEdges.grounding: Reciprocity of existing edge vmPFC->dACC (DEPENDS_ON). canonical-nodes dACC = M6 'conflict/error monitor', vmPFC = M1 'top-down inhibitory brake'; dorsal and ventromedial anterior cingulate/medial PFC are reciprocally connected (the medial-PFC monitoring-regulation cluster).

proposedRedundantPaths.aroundNode: STRI / GP (serial bridge to the thalamo-sensory-motor cluster)
proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: The whole cluster {THAL, V1, A1, S1, GP, CBLM, LGN, MGN, FEF} reaches the main body ONLY through the serial chain FG->STRI->GP->THAL, making BOTH STRI and GP single points of failure. A direct THAL->dACC edge gives the cluster a second, independent bridge to the main body, de-articulating STRI and GP at once (removing either now leaves the cluster attached via THAL->dACC).
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: The mediodorsal / anterior thalamic nuclei project to the anterior cingulate cortex (canonical thalamo-cingulate projection). canonical-nodes THAL = M4 'gating relay / routing', dACC = M6 'conflict/error monitor'.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Gives the auditory cortex a cortical anchor off the THAL hub, reattaching the auditory island {A1, MGN} to the main body when THAL is removed. Also gives A1 a second edge so it is no longer solely dependent on THAL.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes AI = M10 'interoceptive salience'; auditory cortex projects to the insular cortex (auditory-to-insula projection is documented; the insula integrates auditory salience).

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Gives the visual island {V1, LGN, FEF} a cortical anchor off the THAL hub. A ventral-visual-stream edge V1->FG reattaches the island to the main body when THAL is removed (V1 currently has out-degree 0, so it can only receive from THAL/LGN/FEF).
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes V1 = 'primary visual processing', FG = 'fusiform gyrus — face/object recognition'. V1 projects forward along the ventral visual stream to the fusiform gyrus (canonical V1 -> V2 -> ... -> fusiform object/face pathway).

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: FEF reaches the graph only via FEF->V1, so removing V1 isolates it. A frontal attention-control edge gives FEF a second anchor; removing V1 then leaves FEF attached via dlPFC.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes FEF = 'frontal eye fields — attentional gaze control', dlPFC = executive control. The frontal eye fields and dorsolateral PFC are adjacent frontal nodes co-recruited in the frontoparietal attention-control network with reciprocal connectivity.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: AI splits into TWO leaves on removal: PI (PI->AI only) and NTS (NTS->AI only). This edge reattaches the PI leaf: a posterior-insula -> cingulate interoceptive edge gives PI a second anchor. Paired with the NTS->PVN edge below, it fully de-articulates AI.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes PI = M10 'primary interoception', dACC = M6 conflict monitor / salience hub. Posterior/mid-insula interoceptive signals project to the anterior cingulate as part of the interoception-salience pathway.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Reattaches AI's second leaf, NTS (NTS->AI only). A visceral-afferent -> hypothalamus edge gives NTS a second anchor; removing AI then leaves NTS attached via PVN. Together with PI->dACC this drops AI from the articulation set.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes NTS = M10 'visceral afferent hub'. The nucleus tractus solitarius sends a canonical ascending projection to the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (visceral-afferent -> autonomic/neuroendocrine relay). PVN is already an in-graph node (target of mPFC->PVN, BLA->PVN, HIPP->PVN, LC->PVN; source of PVN->HYPO).

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: The interoceptive island {AI, NTS, PI} reaches the main body only via AI->dACC, so removing dACC isolates the whole island. An anterior-insula -> orbitofrontal edge gives the island a second bridge; removing dACC then leaves {AI, NTS, PI} attached via OFC.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: The anterior insula projects to the orbitofrontal cortex, carrying interoceptive/gustatory signal into valuation (canonical insula->OFC pathway). canonical-nodes AI = M10 interoceptive salience, OFC = M6 valuation.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: The reward island {NAcc, VTA, VP} reaches the main body only via NAcc->OFC, so removing OFC isolates it. A ventromedial-PFC corticostriatal edge gives the island a second bridge to the main body via NAcc; removing OFC then leaves the island attached through vmPFC.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: Ventromedial / medial PFC sends a dense glutamatergic corticostriatal projection to the nucleus accumbens shell (canonical vmPFC->NAcc). canonical-nodes vmPFC = M1 brake, NAcc = M11 reward drive.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Within the reward island NAcc solely attaches VTA and VP. This edge gives VP a second anchor and closes the mesolimbic reward loop VTA->NAcc->VP->VTA (the hedonic-output stage feeds back to regulate the dopamine source). Paired with VTA->OFC below so the island survives NAcc removal.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: In-graph the reward chain VTA->NAcc (excit) and NAcc->VP (inhib) already exists; the ventral pallidum sends GABAergic feedback to VTA (canonical mesolimbic disinhibition loop). canonical-nodes VP = 'ventral pallidum — reward/hedonic output', VTA = M11 'dopamine reward source'. One edge serves both recurrence and redundancy.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Gives the reward island a main-body anchor that does NOT pass through NAcc: a mesocortical dopamine edge VTA->OFC. Combined with VP->VTA, removing NAcc leaves the island attached via VP->VTA->OFC, de-articulating NAcc.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: The ventral tegmental area sends the canonical mesocortical dopaminergic projection to orbitofrontal / prefrontal cortex. canonical-nodes VTA = M11 dopamine reward source, OFC = M6 valuation.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: HPA reaches the graph only via HPA->HIPP, so removing HIPP isolates it. Cortisol also acts on the amygdala, giving HPA a second, well-grounded anchor; removing HIPP then leaves HPA attached via BLA.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: Glucocorticoid (HPA-axis) output acts on the basolateral amygdala via glucocorticoid receptors, enhancing threat processing (textbook stress endocrinology). canonical-nodes BLA = M7 'threat learning/acquisition'. NOTE: canonical-nodes marks HPA as a COMPOSITE view ('not an edge endpoint'); the cleaner long-run fix is to remap HPA to a view rather than treat it as a node.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: PAG reaches the graph only via vmPFC->PAG, so removing vmPFC isolates it. A central-amygdala -> PAG efferent gives PAG a second afferent; removing vmPFC then leaves PAG attached via CeA. Also closes the threat-appraisal -> defensive-output pathway.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes CeA = M7 'phasic fear output'; PAG = M8 'defensive kill/lockdown'. The central-amygdala -> periaqueductal-gray projection is the textbook fear-output pathway.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: FPN reaches the graph only via FPN->dlPFC, so removing dlPFC isolates it. A frontoparietal-control -> cingulo-opercular edge gives FPN a second anchor; removing dlPFC then leaves FPN attached via dACC.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes FPN = composite 'fronto-parietal control network'; dACC = M6 conflict monitor. The frontoparietal control network and the cingulo-opercular/salience system (dACC) are reciprocally coupled dual control networks (Dosenbach dual-networks architecture). NOTE: FPN is a COMPOSITE network node, so this grounding rests on network-level coupling rather than a single-fiber projection.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: HYPO reaches the graph only via PVN->HYPO, so removing PVN isolates it. A hypothalamic-defense -> PAG edge gives HYPO a second anchor; removing PVN then leaves HYPO attached via PAG (which is itself reattached to the main body by the CeA->PAG edge above).
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes HYPO = M3 'homeostatic set-point'; PAG = M8 'defensive kill/lockdown'. The hypothalamic defensive column projects to the periaqueductal gray as the canonical autonomic/defensive descending pathway. NOTE: PVN is not a canonical-nodes endpoint; PVN and HYPO are modelled as a serial HPA cascade, so this reattachment depends on CeA->PAG landing first.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: EXTRA-FAULT FIX (not a classic articulation node). {M1, SMA} is a fully disconnected component at baseline. A corticostriatal edge reattaches the dyad to the main body (STRI is a main-body hub), reducing baseComponents 2->1. Paired with THAL->M1 below so the dyad has TWO independent bridges and STRI does not become a NEW single point of failure.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes SMA = 'supplementary motor — self-initiated action sequencing'; SMA is a principal cortical source of the motor corticostriatal projection to putamen/striatum (canonical). STRI already a hub in-graph.

proposedRedundantPaths.rationale: Second independent bridge for the disconnected {M1, SMA} dyad, so removing STRI does not re-isolate it (prevents SMA->STRI from turning STRI into an even worse single point of failure). Also the canonical final leg of the cortico-basal-ganglia-thalamo-cortical motor loop, whose output limb STRI->GP->THAL is already in-graph.
proposedRedundantPaths.grounding: canonical-nodes THAL = M4 'gating relay / routing', M1 = 'primary motor cortex — motor output'. The ventral-anterior/ventral-lateral thalamus -> M1 projection is the canonical thalamocortical motor relay and the return leg of the BG loop already half-present in-graph (STRI->GP inhib, GP->THAL inhib).

projectedImpact.method: The 25 proposed edges (9 feedback + 16 redundant/reconnection) were appended to a deep copy of law.json in memory and re-scored with assets/js/energy-connectivity-audit.js. law.json itself was NOT modified.

recurrentFraction.note: crosses the 0.2 tree-vs-mesh threshold; the 9 reciprocal pairs are exactly the 9 proposedFeedbackEdges (each is the reverse of a pre-existing edge).

baseComponents.note: the {M1, SMA} dyad is reconnected by SMA->STRI + THAL->M1; the graph becomes a single connected body.

articulationNodes.reason: All three residual articulation points survive solely because a dedicated sensory relay leaf has no second grounded projection target present in the graph, so its redundant path was omitted rather than fabricated: THAL still cuts off S1 and CBLM; V1 still cuts off LGN; A1 still cuts off MGN. This is the exact same honest floor Finance bottomed out at (Finance remained articulate at THAL, V1, A1 for the identical CBLM/LGN/MGN reason). The Law-specific serial-bridge fault (STRI/GP holding the whole sensory cluster) and the two-node reward/interoceptive islands are fully cleared by the grounded edges.

candidates.candidate: redundant path around THAL via a second edge on CBLM
candidates.reason: CBLM reaches the graph only via CBLM->THAL. The thalamus does not project to the cerebellum, and cerebellar cortical input arrives polysynaptically via the pontine nuclei (no direct cortex->CBLM fiber to any in-graph node). No honest second edge, so CBLM stays a leaf of THAL and THAL stays a residual articulation point for it.

candidates.candidate: redundant path around V1 via a second edge on LGN
candidates.reason: LGN is a dedicated retino-recipient thalamic relay whose only cortical target is V1; the pulvinar / superior-colliculus partners that would give it a second grounded projection are not present as nodes in the law graph. LGN stays a leaf of V1.

candidates.candidate: redundant path around A1 via a second edge on MGN
candidates.reason: MGN is a dedicated cochlea-recipient (medial geniculate) auditory thalamic relay whose only cortical target is A1; no second grounded projection target exists among the graph's nodes. MGN stays a leaf of A1.

Hippocampal output to lateral PFC is not a monosynaptic projection; direct hippocampal-PFC fibers target mPFC/vmPFC, not dlPFC, and the mPFC relay is not on a law-graph edge path. Cannot ground a direct HIPP->dlPFC edge.

_omittedForLackOfGrounding.notedButNotOmitted: A second anchor for THAL's S1 leaf (S1->M1, densely reciprocal somatomotor connectivity) IS groundable once M1 is reconnected to the main body, but it was NOT added because it would not clear THAL from the articulation set while the ungroundable CBLM leaf persists. It is recorded here as a groundable future edge, not an omission for lack of grounding.
